title: Microsoft Azure Hybrid Cloud
description: Connect office systems and cloud apps with one staff sign-in. A good fit for teams already using Microsoft tools.
steps: Staff sign in with access checks.
Link the office network to Azure.
Host business apps and their data.
Track health and restore lost data.
note: Plan private network access, separate production from testing, and confirm the regions used for data and backups.

title: AWS Customer App Platform
description: Run customer portals, booking systems and mobile backends that need to handle changing demand.
steps: Filter and deliver incoming web traffic.
Keep app records and uploaded files.
note: Use multiple availability zones, private databases, managed secrets and tested restore procedures. Use EKS when Kubernetes is needed.

title: Google Cloud Serverless Apps
description: Build web services and APIs without maintaining application servers. Useful for new services and uneven workloads.
steps: Route requests and apply access rules.
Run an API in managed containers.
Process background work and track health.
note: Set minimum and maximum instances, protect database connections, and check service availability in the chosen region.

title: Private Cloud with OpenShift
description: Run container apps in your own environment or across approved clouds. Useful when location and operating control matter.
steps: Provide the compute and storage base.
note: Allow for platform support, storage resilience, cluster upgrades and a separate recovery location. A cluster alone is not disaster recovery.

title: React and Node.js Web Apps
description: A flexible stack for customer portals, booking tools and internal business dashboards.
steps: Store records and cache frequent reads.
note: Keep permissions in the API, validate inputs, limit requests and decide whether Redis is actually needed.

title: .NET Business Systems
description: Build staff portals and business applications that fit an existing Microsoft environment.
note: Choose managed or self-hosted SQL based on compatibility, licensing and recovery needs. Keep app and database access separate.

title: Java and Spring Business Apps
description: Support transaction-heavy systems, customer services and integration with older enterprise platforms.
note: Start with a modular application when possible. Split into microservices only where independent scaling or ownership justifies it.

title: WordPress and WooCommerce
description: Launch a product catalogue or online store with a familiar content and order management system.
steps: Deliver store pages and filter traffic.
Store orders, media and catalogue data.
Send payment processing to a provider.
note: Use supported plugins, secure admin access, test updates and backups, and use a hosted checkout to reduce card-data exposure.

title: SAP and Business Integration
description: Connect finance, orders and stock data from SAP to customer apps and other business systems.
steps: Map and validate approved API messages.
note: Use supported SAP APIs and business events. Avoid direct writes to ERP tables; confirm licensing and the integration edition needed.

title: Oracle Business Data Integration
description: Connect existing Oracle databases to new portals and reporting tools without replacing the core system.
steps: Serve apps without overloading the core.
note: Use supported APIs for ERP products. Database replication and change capture need version, licensing and load checks.

title: Salesforce Sales and Service
description: Move customer enquiries into sales and service processes, with connections to finance and order systems.
steps: Capture a lead or service request.
Send approved orders and status updates.
note: Agree which system owns each record. Design for API limits, duplicate prevention, customer permissions and integration retries.

title: Workflow Automation with n8n
description: Connect everyday tasks such as invoice follow-up, approval requests and service ticket routing.
steps: Receive a request or system event.
Validate inputs and connect approved tools.
Pause important actions for a decision.
Record the outcome and failed tasks.
note: Protect credentials, verify webhooks, and design safe retries. Use a queue and workers when workload or availability needs grow.

title: Cloud Data Warehouse
description: Bring sales, finance and operations data together so teams can use consistent business reports.
steps: Clean, test and organise reporting tables.
note: Define data owners, access rules and freshness targets. Apply warehouse usage limits and test financial reporting logic.

title: Spark Data Lakehouse
description: Process large files, historical records and mixed datasets for analytics and machine learning.
steps: Land approved data in object storage.
Serve governed analysis and model inputs.
note: Use a data catalogue, access controls, table maintenance and workload limits. Separate sensitive data and manage retention.

title: Kafka Event Processing
description: Share order, stock or payment-status changes between systems without making every app wait for the next one.
steps: Update views and notify other systems.
note: Plan message schemas, ordering, replay and consumer lag. Use idempotent consumers so replay does not create duplicate business actions.

title: Practical Business Dashboards
description: Give growing businesses clear sales and operations reports without starting with a large data platform.
steps: Collect data on an agreed schedule.
Keep reporting separate from live apps.
note: Use read-only reporting access, agree metric definitions and display data freshness. Add a warehouse when scale justifies it.

title: Private Document Assistant
description: Let staff search company manuals and policies using models hosted in your own environment.
steps: Find relevant content the user may access.
Generate an answer using retrieved sources.
Show evidence and flag uncertain answers.
note: Size compute for the chosen model and concurrent users. Test retrieval, access filtering and answer quality; no answer is guaranteed correct.

title: Azure Document AI Assistant
description: Use managed AI and company documents for staff support, with existing Microsoft access controls.
steps: Verify the user and their permissions.
Create a response using retrieved content.
Check quality and retain approved logs.
note: Confirm model and search availability, data processing terms and region. Use private connectivity where supported and validate document permissions.

title: Google Cloud AI Applications
description: Add document search and AI support to customer or staff applications using managed Google Cloud services.
steps: Find relevant content with access filters.
Show sources, collect feedback and logs.
note: Validate the model, retrieval quality, safety rules, regional support and data handling terms before opening access to users.

title: Prediction and ML Serving
description: Deploy demand forecasts, risk scores or image classification models with a controlled release process.
steps: Validate inputs and separate test data.
Train and evaluate a suitable model.
note: Compare against a simple baseline. Monitor drift, response time and business impact; keep rollback and retraining procedures.

title: Infrastructure and GitOps Delivery
description: Build environments and release software through approved, repeatable changes instead of manual server edits.
steps: Apply reviewed app changes to Kubernetes.
note: Protect deployment credentials and Terraform state. Scan images, separate environments and test database migration rollback plans.

title: Monitoring and Service Health
description: See application faults, slow requests and infrastructure issues in one place, with alerts for the right team.
steps: Store metrics, logs and traces separately.
note: Set service targets, useful alert thresholds and retention limits. Remove sensitive fields and control high-cardinality telemetry.

title: Identity and Secure App Access
description: Give staff one controlled way to access internal applications, with multi-factor sign-in and clear permissions.
steps: Verify tokens and enforce app permissions.
note: Single sign-on is one layer of security. Also plan device controls, network restrictions, privileged access and emergency account recovery.

title: Backup and Recovery Foundation
description: Protect databases and business systems, with a recovery plan the team can actually practise.
steps: Identify business systems and recovery order.
Capture consistent backups and transaction logs.
Keep an isolated, immutable copy where supported.
Rebuild systems and verify restored data.
note: Agree recovery time and data-loss targets. Separate backup credentials, keep an offsite copy and schedule full restore exercises.
